adapter_hint: Eurostat NUTS population and median age: python -m scripts.fetch_census.eurostat --level nuts3
religion_basis: survey estimate: self-identification, adults 18+ in private households
religion_note: CBS survey estimate, pooled over 2010-2015 (Kerkelijke gezindte en kerkbezoek naar gemeenten 2010/2015, December 2016, the table behind CBS's paper De religieuze kaart van Nederland, 2010-2015), from the Enquête Beroepsbevolking, the Labour Force Survey, whose 2010-2015 rounds asked about religion: the share of adults aged 18 and over in private households who count themselves to a church denomination or philosophy-of-life group, and which, weighted by CBS. More than 600,000 people answered over the six years; CBS prints a gemeente only when at least 150 respondents stand behind it and does not print the number. The question offered Roman Catholic, Dutch Reformed (Nederlands Hervormd), Reformed (Gereformeerde kerken), the Protestant Church in the Netherlands (PKN, formed from both in 2004; many of its members still name the church they came from), Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and another group; 'Other or unspecified religion' is that last answer, any other church, religion or philosophy of life, which CBS does not divide. 'No religion' is everyone who counts themselves to none. The Netherlands has had no questionnaire census since 1971 and no register records religion; this is CBS's latest table by gemeente (its 2021-2025 survey is published by province and COROP region only). 's-Gravenhage is the gemeente of 2016 itself. CBS does not print the number of respondents; at the survey's national rate (about 549,000 adults over the six years) this gemeente's adults would give about 16,676.
sex_ratio_note: Males per 100 females registered in 's-Gravenhage on 1 January 2022 (CBS key figures by gemeente).
median_age_note: Interpolated within the single year of age that holds the middle person, from CBS's count of the registered population of 's-Gravenhage on 1 January 2022 by sex and single year of age (StatLine 03759ned).
ethnicity_note: Population by migration background on 1 January 2022 (CBS StatLine 84910NED, from the population register): MIGRATION BACKGROUND, not ethnicity, which no Dutch register records. CBS's definition until 2022: a person's own country of birth, or for someone born in the Netherlands the mother's, or the father's where the mother was born in the Netherlands too; 'Dutch' is CBS's Nederlandse achtergrond, both parents born in the Netherlands, whatever the person's nationality. 'Dutch Caribbean' is the former Netherlands Antilles and Aruba as CBS reports them; backgrounds below 0.3% of the country are 'Other migration background'. CBS replaced the classification with 'herkomst' from 2022, and 1 January 2022 is also the date of the division the map draws. Written by the map owner's decision of 19 September 2026.

More than 600,000 people answered over the six years; CBS prints a gemeente only when at least 150 respondents stand behind it and does not print the number. The question offered Roman Catholic, Dutch Reformed (Nederlands Hervormd), Reformed (Gereformeerde kerken), the Protestant Church in the Netherlands (PKN, formed from both in 2004; many of its members still name the church they came from), Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and another group; 'Other or unspecified religion' is that last answer, any other church, religion or philosophy of life, which CBS does not divide. Amersfoort is the gemeente of 2016 itself. CBS does not print the number of respondents; at the survey's national rate (about 549,000 adults over the six years) this gemeente's adults would give about 4,751.

ethnicity_note: Population by migration background on 1 January 2022 (CBS StatLine 84910NED, from the population register): MIGRATION BACKGROUND, not ethnicity, which no Dutch register records. 'Dutch Caribbean' is the former Netherlands Antilles and Aruba as CBS reports them; backgrounds below 0.3% of the country are 'Other migration background'. religion_note: CBS survey estimate, pooled over 2010-2015 (Kerkelijke gezindte en kerkbezoek naar gemeenten 2010/2015, December 2016, the table behind CBS's paper De religieuze kaart van Nederland, 2010-2015), from the Enquête Beroepsbevolking, the Labour Force Survey, whose 2010-2015 rounds asked about religion: the share of adults aged 18 and over in private households who count themselves to a church denomination or philosophy-of-life group, and which, weighted by CBS. More than 600,000 people answered over the six years; CBS prints a gemeente only when at least 150 respondents stand behind it and does not print the number. The question offered Roman Catholic, Dutch Reformed (Nederlands Hervormd), Reformed (Gereformeerde kerken), the Protestant Church in the Netherlands (PKN, formed from both in 2004; many of its members still name the church they came from), Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and another group; 'Other or unspecified religion' is that last answer, any other church, religion or philosophy of life, which CBS does not divide. 'No religion' is everyone who counts themselves to none. The Netherlands has had no questionnaire census since 1971 and no register records religion; this is CBS's latest table by gemeente (its 2021-2025 survey is published by province and COROP region only). Heemskerk is the gemeente of 2016 itself. CBS does not print the number of respondents; at the survey's national rate (about 549,000 adults over the six years) this gemeente's adults would give about 1,284.
sex_ratio_note: Males per 100 females registered in Heemskerk on 1 January 2022 (CBS key figures by gemeente).
median_age_note: Interpolated within the single year of age that holds the middle person, from CBS's count of the registered population of Heemskerk on 1 January 2022 by sex and single year of age (StatLine 03759ned).
ethnicity_note: Population by migration background on 1 January 2022 (CBS StatLine 84910NED, from the population register): MIGRATION BACKGROUND, not ethnicity, which no Dutch register records. CBS's definition until 2022: a person's own country of birth, or for someone born in the Netherlands the mother's, or the father's where the mother was born in the Netherlands too; 'Dutch' is CBS's Nederlandse achtergrond, both parents born in the Netherlands, whatever the person's nationality. 'Dutch Caribbean' is the former Netherlands Antilles and Aruba as CBS reports them; backgrounds below 0.3% of the country are 'Other migration background'. CBS replaced the classification with 'herkomst' from 2022, and 1 January 2022 is also the date of the division the map draws. Written by the map owner's decision of 19 September 2026.

religion_note: CBS survey estimate, pooled over 2010-2015 (Kerkelijke gezindte en kerkbezoek naar gemeenten 2010/2015, December 2016, the table behind CBS's paper De religieuze kaart van Nederland, 2010-2015), from the Enquête Beroepsbevolking, the Labour Force Survey, whose 2010-2015 rounds asked about religion: the share of adults aged 18 and over in private households who count themselves to a church denomination or philosophy-of-life group, and which, weighted by CBS. More than 600,000 people answered over the six years; CBS prints a gemeente only when at least 150 respondents stand behind it and does not print the number. The question offered Roman Catholic, Dutch Reformed (Nederlands Hervormd), Reformed (Gereformeerde kerken), the Protestant Church in the Netherlands (PKN, formed from both in 2004; many of its members still name the church they came from), Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and another group; 'Other or unspecified religion' is that last answer, any other church, religion or philosophy of life, which CBS does not divide. 'No religion' is everyone who counts themselves to none. The Netherlands has had no questionnaire census since 1971 and no register records religion; this is CBS's latest table by gemeente (its 2021-2025 survey is published by province and COROP region only). Horst aan de Maas is the gemeente of 2016 itself. CBS does not print the number of respondents; at the survey's national rate (about 549,000 adults over the six years) this gemeente's adults would give about 1,348.
sex_ratio_note: Males per 100 females registered in Horst aan de Maas on 1 January 2022 (CBS key figures by gemeente).
median_age_note: Interpolated within the single year of age that holds the middle person, from CBS's count of the registered population of Horst aan de Maas on 1 January 2022 by sex and single year of age (StatLine 03759ned).
ethnicity_note: Population by migration background on 1 January 2022 (CBS StatLine 84910NED, from the population register): MIGRATION BACKGROUND, not ethnicity, which no Dutch register records. CBS's definition until 2022: a person's own country of birth, or for someone born in the Netherlands the mother's, or the father's where the mother was born in the Netherlands too; 'Dutch' is CBS's Nederlandse achtergrond, both parents born in the Netherlands, whatever the person's nationality. 'Dutch Caribbean' is the former Netherlands Antilles and Aruba as CBS reports them; backgrounds below 0.3% of the country are 'Other migration background'. CBS replaced the classification with 'herkomst' from 2022, and 1 January 2022 is also the date of the division the map draws. Written by the map owner's decision of 19 September 2026.

More than 600,000 people answered over the six years; CBS prints a gemeente only when at least 150 respondents stand behind it and does not print the number. The question offered Roman Catholic, Dutch Reformed (Nederlands Hervormd), Reformed (Gereformeerde kerken), the Protestant Church in the Netherlands (PKN, formed from both in 2004; many of its members still name the church they came from), Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and another group; 'Other or unspecified religion' is that last answer, any other church, religion or philosophy of life, which CBS does not divide. 'No religion' is everyone who counts themselves to none. The Netherlands has had no questionnaire census since 1971 and no register records religion; this is CBS's latest table by gemeente (its 2021-2025 survey is published by province and COROP region only). Landgraaf is the gemeente of 2016 itself. CBS does not print the number of respondents; at the survey's national rate (about 549,000 adults over the six years) this gemeente's adults would give about 1,271.

religion_note: CBS survey estimate, pooled over 2010-2015 (Kerkelijke gezindte en kerkbezoek naar gemeenten 2010/2015, December 2016, the table behind CBS's paper De religieuze kaart van Nederland, 2010-2015), from the Enquête Beroepsbevolking, the Labour Force Survey, whose 2010-2015 rounds asked about religion: the share of adults aged 18 and over in private households who count themselves to a church denomination or philosophy-of-life group, and which, weighted by CBS. More than 600,000 people answered over the six years; CBS prints a gemeente only when at least 150 respondents stand behind it and does not print the number. The question offered Roman Catholic, Dutch Reformed (Nederlands Hervormd), Reformed (Gereformeerde kerken), the Protestant Church in the Netherlands (PKN, formed from both in 2004; many of its members still name the church they came from), Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and another group; 'Other or unspecified religion' is that last answer, any other church, religion or philosophy of life, which CBS does not divide. 'No religion' is everyone who counts themselves to none. The Netherlands has had no questionnaire census since 1971 and no register records religion; this is CBS's latest table by gemeente (its 2021-2025 survey is published by province and COROP region only). Reimerswaal is the gemeente of 2016 itself. CBS does not print the number of respondents; at the survey's national rate (about 549,000 adults over the six years) this gemeente's adults would give about 670.
sex_ratio_note: Males per 100 females registered in Reimerswaal on 1 January 2022 (CBS key figures by gemeente).
median_age_note: Interpolated within the single year of age that holds the middle person, from CBS's count of the registered population of Reimerswaal on 1 January 2022 by sex and single year of age (StatLine 03759ned).
ethnicity_note: Population by migration background on 1 January 2022 (CBS StatLine 84910NED, from the population register): MIGRATION BACKGROUND, not ethnicity, which no Dutch register records. CBS's definition until 2022: a person's own country of birth, or for someone born in the Netherlands the mother's, or the father's where the mother was born in the Netherlands too; 'Dutch' is CBS's Nederlandse achtergrond, both parents born in the Netherlands, whatever the person's nationality. 'Dutch Caribbean' is the former Netherlands Antilles and Aruba as CBS reports them; backgrounds below 0.3% of the country are 'Other migration background'. CBS replaced the classification with 'herkomst' from 2022, and 1 January 2022 is also the date of the division the map draws. Written by the map owner's decision of 19 September 2026.

religion_note: CBS survey estimate, pooled over 2010-2015 (Kerkelijke gezindte en kerkbezoek naar gemeenten 2010/2015, December 2016, the table behind CBS's paper De religieuze kaart van Nederland, 2010-2015), from the Enquête Beroepsbevolking, the Labour Force Survey, whose 2010-2015 rounds asked about religion: the share of adults aged 18 and over in private households who count themselves to a church denomination or philosophy-of-life group, and which, weighted by CBS. More than 600,000 people answered over the six years; CBS prints a gemeente only when at least 150 respondents stand behind it and does not print the number. The question offered Roman Catholic, Dutch Reformed (Nederlands Hervormd), Reformed (Gereformeerde kerken), the Protestant Church in the Netherlands (PKN, formed from both in 2004; many of its members still name the church they came from), Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and another group; 'Other or unspecified religion' is that last answer, any other church, religion or philosophy of life, which CBS does not divide. 'No religion' is everyone who counts themselves to none. The Netherlands has had no questionnaire census since 1971 and no register records religion; this is CBS's latest table by gemeente (its 2021-2025 survey is published by province and COROP region only). Sliedrecht is the gemeente of 2016 itself. CBS does not print the number of respondents; at the survey's national rate (about 549,000 adults over the six years) this gemeente's adults would give about 787.
sex_ratio_note: Males per 100 females registered in Sliedrecht on 1 January 2022 (CBS key figures by gemeente).
median_age_note: Interpolated within the single year of age that holds the middle person, from CBS's count of the registered population of Sliedrecht on 1 January 2022 by sex and single year of age (StatLine 03759ned).
ethnicity_note: Population by migration background on 1 January 2022 (CBS StatLine 84910NED, from the population register): MIGRATION BACKGROUND, not ethnicity, which no Dutch register records. CBS's definition until 2022: a person's own country of birth, or for someone born in the Netherlands the mother's, or the father's where the mother was born in the Netherlands too; 'Dutch' is CBS's Nederlandse achtergrond, both parents born in the Netherlands, whatever the person's nationality. 'Dutch Caribbean' is the former Netherlands Antilles and Aruba as CBS reports them; backgrounds below 0.3% of the country are 'Other migration background'. CBS replaced the classification with 'herkomst' from 2022, and 1 January 2022 is also the date of the division the map draws. Written by the map owner's decision of 19 September 2026.

religion_note: CBS survey estimate, pooled over 2010-2015 (Kerkelijke gezindte en kerkbezoek naar gemeenten 2010/2015, December 2016, the table behind CBS's paper De religieuze kaart van Nederland, 2010-2015), from the Enquête Beroepsbevolking, the Labour Force Survey, whose 2010-2015 rounds asked about religion: the share of adults aged 18 and over in private households who count themselves to a church denomination or philosophy-of-life group, and which, weighted by CBS. More than 600,000 people answered over the six years; CBS prints a gemeente only when at least 150 respondents stand behind it and does not print the number. The question offered Roman Catholic, Dutch Reformed (Nederlands Hervormd), Reformed (Gereformeerde kerken), the Protestant Church in the Netherlands (PKN, formed from both in 2004; many of its members still name the church they came from), Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and another group; 'Other or unspecified religion' is that last answer, any other church, religion or philosophy of life, which CBS does not divide. 'No religion' is everyone who counts themselves to none. The Netherlands has had no questionnaire census since 1971 and no register records religion; this is CBS's latest table by gemeente (its 2021-2025 survey is published by province and COROP region only). Tynaarlo is the gemeente of 2016 itself. CBS does not print the number of respondents; at the survey's national rate (about 549,000 adults over the six years) this gemeente's adults would give about 1,046.
sex_ratio_note: Males per 100 females registered in Tynaarlo on 1 January 2022 (CBS key figures by gemeente).
median_age_note: Interpolated within the single year of age that holds the middle person, from CBS's count of the registered population of Tynaarlo on 1 January 2022 by sex and single year of age (StatLine 03759ned).
ethnicity_note: Population by migration background on 1 January 2022 (CBS StatLine 84910NED, from the population register): MIGRATION BACKGROUND, not ethnicity, which no Dutch register records. CBS's definition until 2022: a person's own country of birth, or for someone born in the Netherlands the mother's, or the father's where the mother was born in the Netherlands too; 'Dutch' is CBS's Nederlandse achtergrond, both parents born in the Netherlands, whatever the person's nationality. 'Dutch Caribbean' is the former Netherlands Antilles and Aruba as CBS reports them; backgrounds below 0.3% of the country are 'Other migration background'. CBS replaced the classification with 'herkomst' from 2022, and 1 January 2022 is also the date of the division the map draws. Written by the map owner's decision of 19 September 2026.

More than 600,000 people answered over the six years; CBS prints a gemeente only when at least 150 respondents stand behind it and does not print the number. adapter_hint: Eurostat NUTS population and median age: python -m scripts.fetch_census.eurostat --level nuts3
religion_basis: survey estimate: self-identification, adults 18+ in private households
religion_note: CBS survey estimate, pooled over 2010-2015 (Kerkelijke gezindte en kerkbezoek naar gemeenten 2010/2015, December 2016, the table behind CBS's paper De religieuze kaart van Nederland, 2010-2015), from the Enquête Beroepsbevolking, the Labour Force Survey, whose 2010-2015 rounds asked about religion: the share of adults aged 18 and over in private households who count themselves to a church denomination or philosophy-of-life group, and which, weighted by CBS. More than 600,000 people answered over the six years; CBS prints a gemeente only when at least 150 respondents stand behind it and does not print the number. The question offered Roman Catholic, Dutch Reformed (Nederlands Hervormd), Reformed (Gereformeerde kerken), the Protestant Church in the Netherlands (PKN, formed from both in 2004; many of its members still name the church they came from), Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and another group; 'Other or unspecified religion' is that last answer, any other church, religion or philosophy of life, which CBS does not divide. 'No religion' is everyone who counts themselves to none. The Netherlands has had no questionnaire census since 1971 and no register records religion; this is CBS's latest table by gemeente (its 2021-2025 survey is published by province and COROP region only). Voorst is the gemeente of 2016 itself. CBS does not print the number of respondents; at the survey's national rate (about 549,000 adults over the six years) this gemeente's adults would give about 778.
sex_ratio_note: Males per 100 females registered in Voorst on 1 January 2022 (CBS key figures by gemeente).
median_age_note: Interpolated within the single year of age that holds the middle person, from CBS's count of the registered population of Voorst on 1 January 2022 by sex and single year of age (StatLine 03759ned).
ethnicity_note: Population by migration background on 1 January 2022 (CBS StatLine 84910NED, from the population register): MIGRATION BACKGROUND, not ethnicity, which no Dutch register records. CBS's definition until 2022: a person's own country of birth, or for someone born in the Netherlands the mother's, or the father's where the mother was born in the Netherlands too; 'Dutch' is CBS's Nederlandse achtergrond, both parents born in the Netherlands, whatever the person's nationality. 'Dutch Caribbean' is the former Netherlands Antilles and Aruba as CBS reports them; backgrounds below 0.3% of the country are 'Other migration background'. CBS replaced the classification with 'herkomst' from 2022, and 1 January 2022 is also the date of the division the map draws. Written by the map owner's decision of 19 September 2026.

'Dutch Caribbean' is the former Netherlands Antilles and Aruba as CBS reports them; backgrounds below 0.3% of the country are 'Other migration background'.
